mcq.q: Neha promises to pay Om ₹50,000 if Om's house is burnt within a year. This is:
mcq.explain: Section 31 defines a contingent contract as a contract to do or not do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen. Contracts of insurance and indemnity are typical examples. Neha's promise depends on an uncertain future event collateral to the contract, so it is contingent.
mcq.fast: Insurance/indemnity-type promise on a collateral uncertain event = contingent.

mcq.q: Jaya agrees to pay Kunal ₹1 lakh if Kunal marries Lata. Lata dies unmarried. The contract:
options: Becomes void — the event has become impossible (Section 32)
mcq.explain: Section 32 provides that a contract contingent on the happening of an uncertain future event cannot be enforced unless the event happens, and becomes void if the event becomes impossible. Kunal can no longer marry Lata after her death, so the contract becomes void.
mcq.fast: Contingent on HAPPENING + event impossible = void.

mcq.q: Ramesh promises to pay Suresh ₹10,000 if a certain ship does NOT return. The ship sinks. The contract:
mcq.explain: Section 33: if a promise depends on an event NOT occurring, it becomes enforceable only once the event can no longer occur. Once the ship sinks it can never return, so the condition is fulfilled and Suresh can enforce the promise.
mcq.fast: Contingent on NOT happening + happening impossible = enforceable.

mcq.q: Which statement about a contingent contract and a wagering agreement is correct?
options: A contingent contract is valid, whereas a wagering agreement is void
A wagering agreement always has a collateral event; a contingent contract never does
mcq.explain: A contingent contract is valid and enforceable when the condition is met (Sections 31–36). A wagering agreement is void under Section 30. Every wager is in a sense contingent on an event, but not every contingent contract is a wager; in a wager the parties have no interest beyond the bet itself.

mcq.q: Tara pays the municipal tax due on Usha's house to prevent the house, in which Tara has a mortgage interest, from being auctioned. Tara can recover the amount from Usha under:
mcq.explain: Section 69 protects a person who, having an interest of his own, pays money that someone else was legally bound to pay; he can recover it from that other person. Tara's interest as mortgagee made her pay to protect the property, so she is entitled to reimbursement from Usha.
mcq.topic: Necessaries and payments by an interested person (Sections 68 and 69)
mcq.fast: Paid someone else's dues to protect your own interest = 69.

mcq.q: A trader leaves goods at Vijay's shop by mistake. Vijay uses them as his own. Under Section 70, Vijay must:
options: Pay nothing — there was no contract
Pay for the goods, since he enjoyed the benefit of a non-gratuitous delivery
Pay only if he signed a receipt
mcq.explain: Section 70 applies when a person lawfully does something for, or delivers something to, another, not intending to do so gratuitously, and the other enjoys the benefit. The other must compensate or restore the thing. Vijay treated the goods as his own, so he must pay for them.
mcq.topic: Non-gratuitous acts, finder of goods, mistake and coercion (Sections 70 to 72)
mcq.fast: Section 70 test: lawful act, not gratuitous, benefit enjoyed -> pay.

mcq.q: Money paid by mistake must be repaid by the person who received it under:
mcq.explain: Under Section 72, whoever receives money or goods because of a mistake or coercion has to give them back. This applies to a mistake of fact and has been applied by courts to a mistake of law too, for instance tax paid under a law later declared invalid.
mcq.topic: Non-gratuitous acts, finder of goods, mistake and coercion (Sections 70 to 72)
